globalFindings.title: Critical-risk mods block unattended conversion
globalFindings.action: Process critical artifacts individually with source recovery, exact API evidence, transformation audits, and real runtime tests before enabling a batch migration.

globalFindings.title: Different class implementations share one classpath name
globalFindings.action: Relocate the private library or reconcile the implementations; classpath order is not a safe compatibility strategy.

globalFindings.title: Duplicate mod ID is provided by multiple JARs
globalFindings.action: Resolve the canonical artifact and remove or merge only after comparing versions, providers, embedded libraries, and dependent requirements.

globalFindings.title: Required dependencies form a cycle
globalFindings.action: Resolve the cycle as one coordinated compatibility unit. Rebuild or replace the participating versions together, then verify initialization order and runtime behavior.

globalFindings.title: The instance changes loader ecosystems
globalFindings.action: Resolve each project to a native target build first. Port source where no maintained build exists, and use runtime bridges only as separately tested compatibility options.

globalFindings.title: The migration includes a legacy Minecraft toolchain boundary
globalFindings.action: Use era-specific source reconstruction, mappings, build plugins, Java/runtime bootstraps, and compatibility patches. Keep runtime modernization, source porting, and data migration as separate verified deliverables.

globalFindings.title: Some installed mods do not declare source provenance
globalFindings.evidence: 2 mod(s) need source resolution or controlled decompilation
globalFindings.action: Resolve repository lineage through provider metadata and release records. Keep decompiled-source uncertainty explicit.

migrationPlan.title: Snapshot the complete instance
migrationPlan.action: Record the launcher/profile, Minecraft, loader, Java, full mod inventory, configs, scripts, datapacks, resource packs, world copies, hashes, and known runtime baseline before changing anything.
migrationPlan.why: Compatibility work must be recoverable and measured against a known-good baseline.

migrationPlan.title: Resolve every mod to canonical project and source identity
migrationPlan.action: Use cryptographic provider matches, embedded project URLs, release metadata, repository tags, and dependency declarations. Keep forks, ports, and substitutions explicit rather than silently merging identities.
migrationPlan.why: A correct converter cannot patch the wrong project lineage.

migrationPlan.title: Build the complete dependency and incompatibility graph
migrationPlan.action: Combine embedded metadata, provider requirements, optional dependencies, runtime-discovered class links, mixin targets, services, nested JARs, configuration contracts, and known repair records.
migrationPlan.why: Version migration is a graph problem; resolving one JAR in isolation can break its dependents.

migrationPlan.title: Run a dedicated legacy reconstruction and compatibility program
migrationPlan.action: Reproduce the original historical workspace first, then port through explicit source/mapping/data steps. Test Cleanroom, Fugue, MixinBooter, UniMixins, LWJGL3ify, LegacyFix, or other runtime compatibility layers only in separate copied profiles with exact mod/version evidence.
migrationPlan.why: Old mappings, launchers, coremods, Java assumptions, natives, and APIs cannot be safely inferred from modern Loom or NeoForge workflows.

migrationPlan.title: Execute the ordered conversion program
migrationPlan.action: Port libraries and APIs before dependents, then performance/core transformers, content mods, integrations, client-only visuals, and final packs. Preserve a verified artifact at every layer.
migrationPlan.why: Topological ordering reduces repeated failures and makes root causes attributable.

migrationPlan.title: Validate bridge-based compatibility separately
migrationPlan.action: Where relevant, test maintained compatibility layers such as Sinytra Connector, Forgified Fabric API, Kilt, or loader-specific bridges in an isolated profile. Never treat one successful launch as proof of full behavior.
migrationPlan.why: A bridge can save a source port, but it also adds transformation and API-emulation failure modes.

migrationPlan.title: Run clean client, server, world, and feature regression matrices
migrationPlan.action: Use fresh instances, exact rebuilt artifacts, startup and gameplay reproducers, GameTests, log classification, restart persistence, protocol checks, and before/after performance evidence.
migrationPlan.why: The migration is complete only when the real user workflows work without replacement failures.

migrationPlan.title: Deploy transactionally with rollback
migrationPlan.action: Stage every artifact, verify hashes and embedded metadata, back up the existing mod set, apply in dependency order, launch, and roll back the entire batch if validation fails.
migrationPlan.why: Batch updates must never leave the instance in a half-migrated state.

reasons: The artifact declares a source repository.
A reproducible, era-correct source build can expose compiler, mapping, loader, data, and runtime API failures directly.
Runtime modernization and compatibility layers remain separate candidates until the source/data migration is independently proven.

findings.title: Different class implementations share one classpath name
findings.action: Relocate the private library or reconcile the implementations; classpath order is not a safe compatibility strategy.

findings.title: Installed artifact targets a different loader
findings.action: Resolve a native target-loader build or perform a source migration. Test runtime bridges only in an isolated compatibility profile.

findings.title: Required dependency is missing
findings.action: Resolve an exact compatible dependency build or port the dependency first; never delete the declaration merely to force loading.

findings.title: Embedded Minecraft constraint excludes the target release
findings.action: Port and rebuild against the target Minecraft APIs and data formats. Do not broaden metadata until compile and runtime verification pass.

findings.title: Loader APIs and metadata must be migrated
findings.action: Migrate mod metadata, event bus/lifecycle hooks, registries, networking, config, capabilities/attachments, access transformers, Gradle plugin, and loader-specific imports. Compile against both APIs to expose semantic differences.

findings.title: Minecraft API and data migration is required
findings.action: Port one adjacent release boundary at a time, compile and launch at each checkpoint, and preserve a reversible commit for every successful hop.

findings.title: Source location is declared
findings.action: Verify that the repository and tag reproduce this exact JAR before editing.

findings.title: Target Minecraft uses a newer Java toolchain
findings.evidence: JAR max Java 17; target runtime Java 21
findings.action: Move the Gradle toolchain and CI matrix to the target Java version, then compile and run tests under that JVM.

plan.title: Preserve and fingerprint the exact original
plan.action: Copy the JAR to an immutable job workspace, retain its enabled/disabled state, record SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512, archive entry list, metadata, signatures, and dependency graph.
plan.why: Every later edit must be reversible and attributable to this exact input.

plan.title: Reproduce the upstream source build
plan.action: Resolve the declared repository, exact release/tag/commit, mappings, loader, Gradle wrapper, and dependency lock state. Build until the output's metadata and behavior match the installed JAR.
plan.why: A source port is safest when the starting build is reproducible.

plan.title: Separate legacy source reconstruction from runtime compatibility
plan.action: Treat 1.12.2/forge -> 1.21.1/neoforge as three independent tracks: reproduce or reconstruct source with the correct historical mappings and build system; port the code and data contracts; then test optional modern-Java or loader compatibility layers in a copied profile. Never report a runtime bridge as a completed source port.
plan.why: Minecraft 1.7.10, 1.12.2, beta/classic, Legacy Fabric, and Ornithe ecosystems use materially different launchers, mappings, transformers, Java assumptions, and build pipelines.

plan.title: Create the exact target toolchain
plan.action: Create a clean target branch using Minecraft 1.21.1, neoforge, Java 21, era-correct loader build tooling, and exact mappings/dependencies. Do not edit only the JAR metadata.
plan.why: The compiler and loader must expose every API break before runtime.

plan.title: Port through adjacent Minecraft boundaries
plan.action: Generate an ordered migration chain from the source release to the target. Apply one release primer/change set at a time, compile, run static checks, and checkpoint before the next hop. For legacy ranges, generate private mapped/decompiled history with the correct manifest and mapping source rather than extrapolating modern changelogs backwards.
plan.why: Large jumps hide which release removed or changed a symbol, registry, codec, network contract, launcher behavior, or data format.

plan.title: Port loader contracts
plan.action: Migrate mod metadata, event bus/lifecycle hooks, registries, networking, config, capabilities/attachments, access transformers, Gradle plugin, and loader-specific imports. Compile against both APIs to expose semantic differences.
plan.why: Loader metadata, lifecycle, registries, networking, config, capabilities/components, rendering hooks, and distribution rules are not interchangeable.

plan.title: Apply provable source transformations
plan.action: Use compiler diagnostics plus OpenRewrite, JavaParser, Spoon, or focused AST transforms for mechanical API moves. Require a rule test and before/after diff for every transformation family.
plan.why: AST-aware changes scale across a codebase without unsafe global text replacement.

plan.title: Drive the API compatibility loop to zero errors
plan.action: Compile, classify each missing class/method/field/descriptor, inspect both source and target APIs, apply the smallest semantic replacement, and record the mapping in the conversion knowledge base.
plan.why: The compiler and binary API diff are higher-confidence evidence than permissive dependency ranges.

plan.title: Run the real runtime matrix
plan.action: Launch the exact rebuilt artifact on client and dedicated server where applicable, run GameTests/unit tests, exercise original features, inspect fresh logs, restart, and verify persistence and networking. Run runtime bridges and legacy compatibility layers as separate matrix variants, never as hidden dependencies of the source-port result.
plan.why: Static analysis and compilation cannot prove loader bootstrap, mixins, rendering, world data, native libraries, or protocol behavior.

plan.title: Package, diff, and publish provenance
plan.action: Create fresh native-loader JARs, test ZIP integrity, compare entries/resources against the source artifact, scan dependencies, generate checksums/SBOM, install into fresh instances, and retain the complete build receipt. Shade only plain Java libraries; retain native outputs before optionally merging multi-loader artifacts.
plan.why: The final artifact must be reproducible, attributable, and proven to load instead of merely compiling.
